messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming stalls detected for pool=dedicated-chat-prod-us-west-2, model=redwood-chat-v2-4096-q4. p99 = 5.6s (SLO target 1.5s). spike started at ~1728502400 and is ongoing. Queue depth for pool = 84 (normal < 20).

Alex (oncall): I’m paged, taking. priya tagged as next. quick check: any deploys around 17:50?

OpsBot: deploy-bot: No deploys in the last 30m for service=runtime-ingress or pool-controller.

Jon (sre): seeing a pattern: scale-up latencies in autoscaler logs. handshake duration to new node is 45-120s (normal < 8s). warmup registrations failing intermittently.

Carla (runtime): looking at worker logs — new GPU workers boot fine but runtime-agent fails registration due to timeout on kv-cache init. stack shows NFS mount timeouts for /var/cache/kv.

Sasha (eng-runtime): that’s odd — NFS mounts usually stable. can someone paste the autoscaler events and the pool-controller logs?

Alex (oncall): grabbing events:
```
kubectl -n redwood get nodes --selector=pool=dedicated-chat-prod -o wide
# shows nodes in NotReady briefly, then Ready
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/pool-controller | tail -n 200
# events: ScaleUp requested x5, allocations delayed by warmup handshake timeouts
```

Priya (oncall-next): FYI I’m stepping in if this goes >30m, can help runbook actions.

Mikhail (cs): customers reporting streaming stalls and partial responses to chat APIs. A few mid-market customers saw explicit timeouts. raising customer impact: some high-traffic tenants had >10% requests with truncated streams.

Jon (sre): metrics snapshot:
- pool queue depth: peak 112 -> 84 now
- p95 generation time: 780ms -> 2.8s
- p99: 5.6s
- new worker registration latency (median): 48s

Carla (runtime): digging into kv-cache init logs on a failed worker:
```
2026-03-15T17:47:52Z runtime-agent ERROR kvcache: mount failed: timeout waiting for NFS mount
2026-03-15T17:47:53Z runtime-agent WARN warmup: handshake failed, retrying
```
Looks like workers are waiting on NFS which blocks warmup and the worker never registers to the pool. autoscaler thinks it scaled but capacity isn't usable.

Sasha (eng-runtime): is this the same NFS server that had elevated IO earlier today from embeddings jobs? if so, noisy neighbor could explain the mount delay.

Alex (oncall): good call. Jon — can you check storage metrics for nfs-export-3 in us-west-2?

Jon (sre): fetching... yes, NFS export `nfs-export-3` has a sudden IOPS spike starting 17:44 and sustained latency ~350ms (normal 10-20ms). correlates exactly with worker warmup window.

Alex (oncall): root cause candidate: NFS I/O spike causing runtime-agent kv-cache mount timeouts -> worker warmup registration delayed -> autoscaler sees slow registration and queues requests -> queue depth grows -> p99 spikes.

Carla (runtime): mitigation options:
- immediate: disable kv-cache mount during warmup (fastest path) so agents register without blocking, followed by background cache warm.
- fallback: route best-effort traffic to hosted fallback model (lower throughput) for affected customers.
- longer: move KV cache to local SSD on workers or use per-node ephemeral cache to avoid NFS dependency for warmup.

Alex (oncall): immediate plan: try toggle to skip kv-cache mount at warmup on a subset of new nodes (canary 2 nodes) and observe registration. will push change via pool-controller config. Carla, can you prepare config?

Carla (runtime): on it. preparing patch to set env WARMP_SKIP_KVCACHE=true for warmup container. will apply to a single zone subset first.

Sasha (eng-runtime): also prepare a routing fallback to route tier=best-effort to hosted-chat-1 for customers who opt-in; should reduce load while we fix.

Alex (oncall): executing canary now.

OpsBot: ops-bot: Applying patch to pool-controller namespace...

Carla (runtime): patch applied to canary subset. watching registration.

Jon (sre): new workers in canary registered in ~6s. queue depth trending down (84 -> 46 in 4 minutes). p99 dropped to 2.1s.

Mikhail (cs): passing to CS: customers on affected tenants seeing improvement in streaming. one tenant still reports intermittent stalls, but overall reduced.

Alex (oncall): good. start rolling to additional nodes in pool in controlled increments. keep WARMP_SKIP_KVCACHE on until NFS IOPS normalized.

Sasha (eng-runtime): I’ll open a follow-up PR to change warmup semantics permanently to avoid synchronous NFS mount. Suggest background populate cache after worker registers.

Jon (sre): storage team alerted to noisy neighbor on nfs-export-3. they’re investigating top talkers; will throttle or migrate offending jobs.

Carla (runtime): adding temporary runbook note: "If kv-cache mount fails during warmup -> set WARMP_SKIP_KVCACHE on warmup flow and scale up nodes; monitor registration latency."

Alex (oncall): Customer impact: intermittent streaming stalls and truncated responses for ~37 minutes across 3 tenants, top impacted tenant saw 12% error rate during the peak window. Logging ticket INC-2026-789 created. tagging customers and sending update.

Mikhail (cs): I’ll draft customer comms and coordinate with legal for any SLA implications.

Priya (oncall-next): I’m taking over monitoring for the remainder of the shift. Alex — anything you want handed off?

Alex (oncall): handoff: WARMP_SKIP_KVCACHE is enabled for pool. storage team will confirm nfs-export-3 mitigation. follow steps in runbook, if p99 > 3s re-escalate to eng-runtime and oncall-sre. update INC-2026-789 with timeline and mitigations.

Priya (oncall-next): ack. I’ll watch dashboards and coordinate with storage.

Sasha (eng-runtime): follow-up action items (tracking):
- short: make warmup asynchronous from kv-cache mount (owner: eng-runtime, Carla)
- mid: migrate critical KV workloads off nfs-export-3 or provide rate limits (owner: eng-infra, Jon)
- long: evaluate local SSD cache design to remove NFS dependency for warmup (owner: eng-runtime)

Alex (oncall): adding note: avoid full pool-wide rollback; we did canary -> partial -> roll. good ops choreography. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Status update posted to INC-2026-789. Severity: Sev2. Current status: mitigated (partial); monitoring.

Mikhail (cs): customers updated, CS queue cleared for priority tenants, will follow up with RCA once ready.

Jon (sre): storage team pinned root cause to an adhoc batch job misconfigured for export `nfs-export-3`. they applied throttling and moved heavy jobs to a different export. NFS latency restored to normal at 17:59.

Priya (oncall-next): I’m keeping handoff watch for 1h. if all metrics stable and p99 < 1.8s for 30m, I’ll mark incident resolved.

Carla (runtime): PR opened to make warmup kv-cache optional and to background populate. link: https://git.internal.redwood/p/runtime/pull/4523

Alex (oncall): Thanks all. leaving notes in INC-2026-789 and linking to this thread. good response.

Sasha (eng-runtime): will work with infra on the SSD cache proposal next sprint.

IncidentBot: update: last alert cleared at 1728503580. incident remains open for RCA and follow-ups.

Alex (oncall): closing primary paging loop. Priya takes post-incident watch. good job team. :clap:
